title: Trump Rejects Iranian Ceasefire Offer, Signals Post-Midterm Resumption of Strikes
snippet: President Donald Trump has turned down a seven-day ceasefire proposal from Tehran, reportedly informing aides that U.S. bombing operations against Iran are expected to resume following the November midterm elections.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has rejected a proposed seven-day ceasefire from Tehran and indicated to senior aides that U.S. military strikes against Iran are likely to resume after the November midterm elections, according to sources familiar with the administration's internal deliberations.

The Iranian proposal, presented by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi through Qatari intermediaries, offered to halt hostilities and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz. In return, Tehran demanded that Washington lift its naval blockade on Iranian ports, waive sanctions on petroleum exports, and include Lebanon in the cessation of conflict. Iranian leaders framed the seven-day window as a stepping stone toward comprehensive talks over their nuclear program.

Backchannel Diplomacy in New York

The diplomatic maneuver coincided with the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where U.S. and Iranian officials engaged in indirect contact. Key figures involved in the deliberations included U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Although Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged that a lengthy mediated session failed to produce a breakthrough, Iranian negotiators expressed openness to continued discussions.

Divergent Timelines for Resolution

The conflict has exacerbated volatility in global energy markets, largely due to ongoing threats to shipping corridors in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has pressed for an agreement prior to the November vote in the U.S. to prevent further economic distress and military escalation.

However, Trump has held firm on his timeline, telling audiences at the UN General Assembly that he expects a final resolution only after the midterm elections. While holding out the possibility of a deal, Trump warned that a failure to reach terms would result in a swift and expanded U.S. military response.
